study_identification_part.si4_title: Normative modeling of brain MRI data identifies small subcortical volumes and associations with cognitive function in youth with fetal alcohol spectrum disorder (FASD)

cm1_research_objectives.reason: The study clearly states its hypotheses and objectives. It hypothesizes that regional subcortical volume z-scores would be lower for youth with FASD and associated with cognitive function. The purpose is to quantify these anomalies and assess sensitivity/specificity.
cm1_research_objectives.supporting_text:
We hypothesized: 1) regional subcortical volume zscores would be lower for youth with FASD... 2) youth with FASD would demonstrate betweengroup regional variability... and 3) larger subcortical volume z-scores would be associated with better neurocognitive and neurobehavioral functioning.
Aim: To quantify regional subcortical brain volume anomalies in youth with fetal alcohol spectrum disorder (FASD), assess the relative sensitivity and specificity of abnormal volumes in FASD vs. a comparison group, and examine associations with cognitive function.

nm1_selection_criteria_reference_cohort.reason: The study uses an existing normative model (CentileBrain). It cites the original publication and reports the total sample size of the reference cohort (37,407). However, it does not explicitly detail the eligibility criteria or quality standards for the CentileBrain reference cohort itself in the text, relying on the citation.
nm1_selection_criteria_reference_cohort.supporting_text: Individual regional volumetric z-scores were generated using CentileBrain (Ge et al., 2024), an open source online software tool that leverages an aggregated neuroimaging dataset with a large number of individuals (37,407 comparison brains).

cr1_selection_criteria_clinical_cohort.reason: The study clearly describes eligibility criteria for both the FASD group (documented heavy PAE, IOM criteria) and the comparison group (no neuro/dev disorders). It specifies image quality standards (visual inspection, Euler value thresholds) and reports final sample sizes and exclusion reasons.
cr1_selection_criteria_clinical_cohort.supporting_text: Exclusion criteria... included neurological and developmental disorders... To be eligible for the FASD group, documented evidence of heavy PAE was required... Eight participants (6 comparison, 2 FASD) were excluded due to excess head motion... Total of 86 participants were included (FASD = 47, comparison = 39).

cr2_handling_of_clinical_covariates.reason: The study considers clinical covariates. It specifically tested for the confounding effects of 'other substance exposure' (polysubstance) and found no significant differences, so it was excluded from further analysis. It also examined associations with dysmorphic facial features.
cr2_handling_of_clinical_covariates.supporting_text: To test for potential confounding effects of prenatal substance exposures in addition to alcohol... we used independent samples t-tests... Because it was not a confounding variable, other substance exposure was not included in any subsequent analyses.
cr2_handling_of_clinical_covariates.location: Methods 2.6 Statistical analysis; Results 3.1 Subject characteristics
